note: One move, a slide into the next position and a bend at the end of the phrase: the crossing from position 1 to 2 with the slide's notes ringed, the bend held against a drone on the root, then the same move at the next crossing. Moves holds any key, so the text names the key as a param and the last line says what stays the same in another key.

exercise.title: Slide in, bend out
exercise.why: A slide takes your hand into the next position and a bend finishes the phrase there, so the two together are one move you can use at every crossing.

cells.text:
The neck below shows only the crossing from position 1 to position 2 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale. Climb position 1 from the low E string, and on the G string slide from the ringed {{4}} up to the ringed {{5}}. You are now in position 2: on the B string, bend {{b7}} up until it sounds like the {{1}} next to it.
Practice until the slide and the bend feel like one phrase.

Press Play below to start the drone on {{=key}}, and play the move again. The bend ends on the drone's own note, so hold it at the top and listen for the two to settle into one sound.
If the bend stops short, push a little further and listen again.

Now the same move at the next crossing. Climb position 2 and slide up the G string from the ringed {{5}} to the ringed {{b7}} into position 3. On the high e string, bend {{4}} up until it sounds like {{5}}.
Practice until the bend reaches its note without you checking the drone.
{{?key}}In another key the move sits on other frets, and both slides are still on the G string.
